name: Sourdough
line: Our twelve-year-old starter, a long rest, and a dark, crackling crust.
about: Each loaf rests a full day before it goes in the oven at four, so it's sour, chewy, and keeps for days.

name: Dark rye
line: Rye, caraway and a little molasses, dense and dark.
about: Slice it thin. It keeps for a week, and it's best with butter and a little salt.

name: Seeded
line: Sunflower, pumpkin, flax and sesame, inside and on top.
about: A wholemeal dough with four kinds of seeds, toasted first, so the whole loaf tastes nutty.

name: Baguette
line: Crisp outside, open and soft inside, baked three times a day.
about: Best within a few hours, which is why we bake them at seven, at eleven and at three.
